Determine if TOC removal meets Stage 1 DBP Rule requirements

Source: R/regulate_toc.R
regulate_toc.Rd

This function takes raw water alkalinity, raw water TOC, and finished water TOC. It then calculates the TOC removal percentage and checks compliance with the Stage 1 DBP Rule.

Usage

regulate_toc(
  alk_raw,
  toc_raw,
  toc_finished,
  raw_water,
  treated_water,
  skip_alternate = FALSE
)

regulate_toc_df(
  df,
  alk_raw = "use_col",
  toc_raw = "use_col",
  toc_finished = "use_col",
  input_raw_water = "defined",
  input_treated_water = "treated",
  skip_alternate = FALSE
)

Arguments

alk_raw

Raw water alkalinity (mg/L as calcium carbonate). Not needed if waters are provided.

toc_raw

Raw water total organic carbon (mg/L). Not needed if waters are provided.

toc_finished

Finished water total organic carbon (mg/L). Not needed if waters are provided.

raw_water

A water object of class "water" created by define_water() containing raw water parameters. If provided, the function will use the alk and toc slots from this object as inputs. If not provided, alk_raw and toc_raw must be specified.

treated_water

A water object of class "water" created by define_water() containing treated water parameters. If provided, the function will use the toc slot from this object as input for finished water TOC. If not provided, toc_finished must be specified.

skip_alternate

Logical value indicating whether to skip alternative compliance checks. By default, alternative compliance will be checked.

df

a data frame optionally containing columns for raw water alkalinity, raw water TOC, and finished water TOC

input_raw_water

a name of the column of water class data to be used as the input raw water for this function. Default is "defined".

input_treated_water

a name of the column of water class data to be used as the input treated water for this function. Default is "treated".

Value

A data frame containing the TOC removal compliance status, and a comment with the reasoning for the compliance status.

A data frame with compliance status, removal percent, and optional note columns.

Details

The function prints the input parameters and the calculated removal percentage for TOC. It checks compliance with regulations considering the raw TOC, alkalinity, and removal percentage. It outputs a dataframe that contains the compliance status as a boolean, calculated removal precent as a numeric, and a comment that indicates internal reasoning for compliance status.

Examples

regulate_toc(alk_raw=50, toc_raw=5, toc_finished=2)
#>   toc_compliance_status toc_removal_percent required_removal
#> 1                  TRUE                  60                0
#>                                                                              comment
#> 1 Treated water TOC < 2 mg/L meets alternative compliance (sect 141.135 (a)(2)(ii)).

water1 <- define_water(alk = 70, toc = 4)
#> Warning: Missing value for `ph`; carbonate balance will not be calculated.
#> Warning: Missing value for `doc`; defaulting to 95% of TOC.
#> Warning: Major ions, TDS, and conductivity are all missing; assuming ideal conditions.
#> Ionic strength will be "NA" and activity coefficients will be 1.
water2 <- define_water(toc = 2.5)
#> Warning: Missing value for `ph`; carbonate balance will not be calculated.
#> Warning: Missing value for `alk`; carbonate balance will not be calculated.
#> Warning: Missing value for `doc`; defaulting to 95% of TOC.
#> Warning: Major ions, TDS, and conductivity are all missing; assuming ideal conditions.
#> Ionic strength will be "NA" and activity coefficients will be 1.
regulate_toc(raw_water = water1, treated_water = water2)
#> Warning: Treated Water DBPs (TTHM or HAA5) are missing. Alternative compliance based on DBPs (sect 141.135 (a)(2)(iii and iv)) may not be applied.
#> Warning: Raw water SUVA is missing or cannot be calculated. Alternative compliance based on SUVA (sect 141.135 (a)(2)(v)) will not be applied.
#> Warning: Treated water SUVA is missing or cannot be calculated. Alternative compliance based on SUVA (sect 141.135 (a)(2)(vi)) will not be applied.
#>   toc_compliance_status toc_removal_percent required_removal
#> 1                  TRUE                37.5               25
#>                   comment
#> 1 Standard compliance met

regulate_toc(raw_water = define_water(alk = 50, toc = 5), 
treated_water = define_water(toc = 2), skip_alternate = TRUE)
#> Warning: Missing value for `ph`; carbonate balance will not be calculated.
#> Warning: Missing value for `doc`; defaulting to 95% of TOC.
#> Warning: Major ions, TDS, and conductivity are all missing; assuming ideal conditions.
#> Ionic strength will be "NA" and activity coefficients will be 1.
#> Warning: Missing value for `ph`; carbonate balance will not be calculated.
#> Warning: Missing value for `alk`; carbonate balance will not be calculated.
#> Warning: Missing value for `doc`; defaulting to 95% of TOC.
#> Warning: Major ions, TDS, and conductivity are all missing; assuming ideal conditions.
#> Ionic strength will be "NA" and activity coefficients will be 1.
#>   toc_compliance_status toc_removal_percent required_removal
#> 1                  TRUE                  60               45
#>                   comment
#> 1 Standard compliance met


regulated <- water_df %>%
  dplyr::select(toc_raw = toc, alk_raw = alk) %>%
  regulate_toc_df(toc_finished = seq(2, 4, 0.1))

regulated <- water_df %>%
  define_water_df() %>%
  chemdose_ph_df(alum = 30, output_water = "dosed") %>%
  chemdose_toc_df("dosed") %>%
  pluck_water(c("coagulated", "defined"), c("toc", "alk")) %>%
  dplyr::select(toc_finished = coagulated_toc, toc_raw = defined_toc, alk_raw = defined_alk) %>%
  regulate_toc_df()
#> Warning: No coagulants dosed; final water will equal input water. (12 rows affected.)

water1<-water_df |> 
 define_water_df() |> 
 chemdose_toc_df(output_water= "dosed", alum=20) |> 
 regulate_toc_df(input_raw_water = "defined", input_treated_water= "dosed")
